blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Salmon River is rural Township of Langley: the Salmon River itself flows north to the Fraser River, and the Township's Rural Plan lists it among the river systems draining the municipality.
The upland house area is named Salmon River Uplands in Township plans, sitting above the river flats between Fort Langley to the northwest and Murrayville to the south.
Williams Park marks the middle of the uplands: 36.5 acres, bounded to the east by 238 Street and to the south by 64 Avenue.

blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are rural residential on large lots: the Township's Official Community Plan (OCP) policy for Salmon River Uplands says the area shall be maintained for rural residential and agricultural uses.
2500, which applies to the whole Township and sets permitted uses, lot coverage and building restrictions parcel by parcel.
Servicing is part of the stock's character: residents not served by the Township water utility get water from private or community wells, per the Township's water quality report.

blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) boundary and the Rural designation do not line up here: the Rural Plan names Salmon River Uplands as an area where the ALR boundary and the OCP designation conflict, to be reviewed with the Agricultural Land Commission.

Streamside Protection and Enhancement Areas (SPEAs) apply outside the ALR: Schedule 3 of the OCP sets non-disturbance zones around watercourses, with setback width set by a Qualified Environmental Professional based on the watercourse class.
Flowing artesian wells are a named local hazard: controlling artesian flow is required under the Water Sustainability Act, Sections 52 and 53, and the Groundwater Protection Regulation.

blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Brown Park, 12.9 acres off 240 Street south of 51 Avenue, is in Salmon River Uplands and runs on its own well, not Township water.
Williams Park and Brown Park wells are tested weekly for E. coli, coliforms, turbidity, temperature and pH, and twice a year for arsenic and other metals.
The Fraser Highway Employment Lands plan area, about 152 hectares (ha) from 228 Street to 240 Street, sits beside Salmon River Uplands and is surrounded by the ALR but includes no ALR land itself.
The Nicomekl River, locally named Hatchery Creek in that plan area, flows west through its northern portion in a ravine between Fraser Highway, 232 Street and 236 Street.
Best Creek, also called Trigg Creek, is a primary tributary to Murray Creek and supports coho salmon and trout, per the same Township reference plan.

blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Well and septic costs sit with the owner here: the Township's water report notes unserviced residents rely on private or community wells, so testing and system replacement are household costs, not utility charges.
Artesian control is also an owner cost risk: the Township warns a flowing artesian well can cause substantial property damage and significant remediation costs if not properly controlled or closed.
Roads are rural grid: the employment lands plan frames the area by Fraser Highway, 48 Avenue, Old Yale Road and 40 Avenue, and Salmon River houses feed into that same grid.
Fort Langley is the service village to the northwest, reached on the rural avenues; its two SD35 schools on Bartlett Street and Trattle Street mark the village core.

blocks.text: Salmon River Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the aquifer map: the Township's artesian advisory maps areas under potential artesian pressure, and a qualified professional or certified well-driller must advise before drilling.
Check ALR status in GeoSource before any use assumption: the Township's application guide tells buyers to determine whether a property is within the ALR as a first review step.
Check the floodplain and the river setback together: the Rural Plan places a floodplain area south and west of Fort Langley in the same drainage system the Salmon River feeds.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Salmon River?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Salmon River?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.
